description.value: This study tested the behavioral and neurobiological impact of acute psychosocial stress on cognitive reappraisal during fMRI.

value: We predicted that acute stress would impair CR success and that it would do so by impacting the adaptive responding of biological systems that are engaged by both CR and stress.

value: No ROI showed a significant interaction between group (stress, control) and reappraisal condition after correcting for multiple comparisons.

Preprocessed images were entered into a standard general linear model in FSL

Preprocessed images were entered into a standard general linear model in FSL, which estimated neural responses to the cue period (collapsed over trial types), the three types of picture periods (decrease-negative, look-negative, and look-neutral), and the rating period (collapsed over trial types).
Regressors used boxcar functions convolved with the canonical double-gamma hemodynamic response function implemented in FSL.

model_settings.value: Motion parameters, temporal derivatives, temporal filter regressors, and censored volumes were included as nuisance regressors.

spans.text: The model also included nuisance regressors for motion parameters, temporal derivatives for each regressor of interest, and temporal filter regressors with a cutoff of 128 sec.
